Change has been successfully rebased and submitted as 2682a0e76f9a77dc42b20d317850277e3ac3a33c
Should we just put these two things in one map instead of maintaining them separately?

I used a separate map to minimize the number of changes. To use currentAggregationSources I would've had to change the type to something like std::unordered_map<std::string, AggregationSrcData> where AggregationSrcData is a struct with fields for url and creds. This would have require to change the usage of currentAggregationSources everywhere. 

Using one map is cleaner though and I can make this change in this patchset or open a new MR with this change

> I used a separate map to minimize the number of changes.

As a general rule, "minimize the size of the changeset" isn't really a goal.  The goal is clean and consistent code.

I don't really care if it's one patchset or two, but I'd like the version that we merge to have a single map.  It also simplifies some of the cleanup because we only have to lookup/delete one thing.

I've added a separate patch handler that allows patching username and password independently. These changes are also part of patchset 13 and we should have the behavior that you described above.
yep, current code looks correct.  value_or isn't something we use often, so I didn't read it right.  Fine as is.
These are coming from a user.  Some level of checking they're sane needs to happen.  They can't include ":", because they're being base64 encoded, and we should enforce some length (40 characters?)
